newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Peters says allegations against Morgan false.
newsitem.headline: NZ Peters says allegations against Morgan false.

text.p: Treasurer Winson Peters said on Thursday said allegations of mispending against MP Tukoroirangi Morgan were false, that his Te Tai Hauauru seat was safe and New Zealand First's coalition with the National Party was rock solid.
Wellington's The Dominion newspaper reported on Thursday Morgan was paid director's wages in September, October and November, totalling $56,250 since resigning as a director on August 30.
Peters said in a Radio NZ interview that allegations against Morgan were disgraceful.
"They make all sorts of allegations and they cannot sheet home one of them because they are false," Peters said.
Peters said Morgan did not receive directors fees after he resigned but received fees for programmes Morgan had been contracted to provide.
"Was he paid directors fees on an on-going basis after he was no longer a director. The answer is categorically 'No'," Peters said.

The Serious Fraud Office has been investigating alleged irregularities in payments to Morgan by ATV and Peters said the SFO investigation was being conducted more competently than any journalists' investigations.
Peters said it was unreasonable for Morgan to be asked to answer allegations for which there was not one shred of evidence.

Asked if the controversy had shaken the coalition government, Peters said: "The coalition is rock solid and no amount of scaremongering on the part of those who would love to be in government and don't deserve to be, is going to change that."
Asked if Morgan's seat was safe, Peters said, "You know it is."
